record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in the Dynamics of Quadratic and Higher Degree Polynomial ODE Systems
record.context_brief: rigorous chaos proofs for four quadratic systems
record.original_question: Give rigorous existence proofs of chaotic solutions for each of the following four three-dimensional quadratic autonomous systems, which were found numerically to have Rössler-type attractors: (i) x' = y^2 - x + Az, y' = x, z' = y; (ii) x' = yz - x + Ay, y' = z, z' = x; (iii) x' = yz + Az, y' = x - y, z' = y; (iv) x' = y^2 + Az, y' = x - y, z' = y.

evidence.quote: ... the following four systems are later studied in our work [Zhang & Heidel, 2010] ... System (3.27) and system (3.28) share the same scalar equation u000 = uu0 - u00 - Au in y and z respectively. The attractors are all of Rössler type. The open problem is to prove rigorously the existence of chaotic solutions in these systems: ... x0 = y 2 - x + Az ... y0 = x ... z 0 = y ... x0 = yz - x + Ay ... y0 = z ... z 0 = x ... x0 = yz + Az ... y0 = x - y ... z 0 = y ... x0 = y 2 + Az ... y0 = x - y ... z 0 = y.

artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not return any rigorous existence proof of chaos specifically for these four three-dimensional quadratic systems. Related work by Heidel and Zhang focuses on classifying non-chaotic quadratic 3D systems, and computer-assisted proofs of chaos exist for the classical Rössler system, but no source explicitly establishes rigorous chaos for the four listed systems.
